correctness.rationale: In a finite local ring every nonzero nonunit is a vertex. The pairing descends over the residue field because multiplying by an element of m changes neither product in m² nor its scalar action. The inverse image of the radical is the socle, with q^(r+1) elements; its nonzero members have annihilator m. All other annihilators are preimages of hyperplanes in V and thus of equal cardinality q^d. Equality of those hyperplanes is equivalent to proportional nonzero images in V/U by nondegeneracy. Counting lifts gives c=q^(r+1)−1, b=(q−1)q^(r+1) and N=(q^t−1)/(q−1). At rank one there is one block; otherwise the c universal vertices and N components of order b are intrinsic. Then q=1+b/(c+1), followed by unique r,t from the two powers. The automorphism group and coloring follow from those intrinsic blocks. A diagonal form of rank t realizes each triple, since all triple products in the maximal ideal vanish. The two ternary forms have the same rank but only the hyperbolic ring has a nonsocle element squaring to zero. No splitting assumption was used in the graph proof.
residual_risks: The script directly compares every adjacency for the split examples, but the mixed examples compare computed degree distributions only, and both lie at rank one. This is narrower than the prose suggesting all mixed edges are compared with the block rule. It does not limit the general proof.

value.rationale: The block structure answers the suggested clique and chromatic questions on a natural family and gives more than those invariants: it separates which residue and rank parameters can be read from the graph from which multiplication data are lost. The mixed-characteristic scope and exact example of lost form data make that distinction useful.
